checks: The finite set of containing base traces has a minimum-weight trace. Moving the boundary of a minimizing cap inward to pass through p cannot increase its weight and remains a containing cap, so the tightened trace is also minimizing. The formal whole-base trace can be represented by zero base normal.

For any fixed continuous unit normal, finiteness of P and compactness of the fibers make a single finite T work for both opposite signs on all nonzero-drift fibers. The two masses are exactly complementary on each zero-drift fiber up to a d-volume-null hyperplane, and both caps are actual nonvertical caps even in base rank zero. Their sum is twice the minimizing base mass less the total zero-drift mass, which is at least V_p. This applies also to y on the own boundary.

Positive homogeneity permits Gamma(u)=1. On the own fiber the base drift vanishes, so the new cap gains the part of the inball with signed Euclidean displacement between -delta/||u|| and zero. Since ||u||<=C, the proposed thickness min(r/2,delta/C) lies within that strip. For distance t<=r/2 from the central section, the sectional radius sqrt(r^2-t^2) is at least sqrt(3)r/2. Fubini proves the displayed volume, including d=1 where the sections have unit zero-dimensional mass. Endpoint choices change no volume.

The base coefficient never enters the own-fiber strip estimate, so the positive gain survives the infimum over arbitrarily large tilts. Pure-base masses are unchanged and exceed D_0 by at least V_p/2. Both terms in the final minimum are strictly positive since r and delta are positive, the unit norm sphere gives C>0, and V_p>0.
